additions.name: Jiujiang University — Danfengyuan Campus Data Centre

status.summary: Jiujiang University’s Danfengyuan data-centre room serves academic affairs, student services, office administration and finance systems. On September 30 the university scheduled an October 2–3 outage to upgrade its aging UPS supply. The room was operating before that planned maintenance; completion of the cutover and subsequent service restoration have not been confirmed.

locator.precision: Representative point inside Jiujiang University’s Danfengyuan campus at 551 Qianjin East Road. It locates the named parent campus, not the data-centre building, room, entrance or a surveyed parcel.
locator.identity_review: The September 30 notice names Danfengyuan campus. The March 11 university tender explicitly identifies that campus at 551 Qianjin East Road. The March 7 university notice places Jingzhi Building (竞知楼) on Danfengyuan and directs entry through the same address. Native OSM places the exact named Jingzhi Building entirely within university way 264303327, while separately naming adjacent Ziweiyuan way 666099948. The selected point is inside the former and outside the latter. The campus map is therefore bridged by primary address and landmark identity, not a generic university name alone. The data-centre building itself remains unidentified.
locator.uncertainty_reason: Community vector geometry supplies no measured positional accuracy; displacement from the campus marker to the unidentified room is unknown.

additions.successor_review: September 30 establishes existing operations through named live services and installed equipment scheduled for shutdown. Its planned October 2–3 cutover is not treated as started, completed or restored merely because time has passed. Exact-title/domain searches and captured current university notices/IT-centre indices found no verified later cutover completion. One existing-room entry absorbs the UPS context; no second project/site is manufactured for maintenance. The separate March electrical-works tender supplies campus address only. The native campus polygon is matched through primary named-building and address evidence; no exact room or building is selected.

additions.name: CEC Tokyo No.2 Existing Operations at Sunshine 60

locator.precision: Community-mapped reference point inside the named Sunshine 60 office tower, the host building for CEC Tokyo No.2. It is not a separately mapped data-center suite, floor, boundary or rack location. The point does not assert that the entire tower is a data center.
locator.identity_review: CEC’s 2010 opening release identifies Tokyo No.2 as the acquired MEX data-center business in Ikebukuro, occupying three floors in a 60-story tower. The current CEC contracts index explicitly maps MEX service to Tokyo No.2. The original legacy MEX facility page names the installation environment as Ikebukuro Sunshine 60. OSM way314155355 independently names exactly Sunshine 60, and the property operator’s access illustration identifies the tower within the complex. No headquarters-only inference or general Sunshine City complex marker is used.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The community geometry has no measured positional-accuracy statement. Decimal precision is not survey accuracy; the source polygon is used only to choose a host-building reference point.

status.summary: CEC operated Tokyo No.2 in Sunshine 60, Ikebukuro, when a service disruption occurred on August 5. It later reported restoring the affected services in a separate environment. CEC plans to move customer equipment by the end of October 2026; completion of the move and closure of the Sunshine 60 facility have not been confirmed.

Recovery notices describe another environment without locating it; the new Tokyo No.3 and hybrid-cloud facilities are not placed here.

context_updates.identity_review: Read the original September 29 interview capture and live original. Named president Ito describes use of abundant Ogaki groundwater to improve air-conditioning efficiency. In response to a GPU-hosting question he reports very few enquiries and says the facilities are not specifically designed for high power density. No numerical PUE or building-specific cooling design is supplied.
context_updates.summary: In an interview published on September 29, 2026, Mirai president Yoshihito Ito said the Ogaki operation uses groundwater to improve cooling efficiency. He described very few GPU-server enquiries and said its facilities were not designed specifically for high power density. These statements concern the Ogaki operation collectively; they do not provide building-specific cooling specifications or a numeric PUE.
